transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well... I guess I finally agreed to come in because things have just been a bit off. I just don't really care about the things that used to keep me balanced. 

Um... sailing races, my Saturday shift at the historical society... even just tinkering out in the woodshop. It all just feels like a chore lately. I just... keep putting it all off.
How long have you been feeling this way?
I suppose... a little over a year now. Ever since the... well, the scaffold accident. We were going through a business readjustment at the time. So, yeah. Just a little over a year.
Do you still enjoy things you used to find pleasure in, or has the pleasure gone away as well?

I guess... yeah, it's mostly gone. Um... even with other things. Like, my wife and kids will be laughing at dinner, or... I'll finish a difficult project milestone at work. I know I should feel good about those things, but... I don't know. I mostly just feel flat. Just sort of... removed from it all, I suppose.
Have you had periods in the past year where you felt really down or depressed, separate from the general feeling of not caring about things?
No, not really. Um... I don't think so, anyway. It's not like I'm sitting around feeling sad or anything like that. It's mostly just... what I said before. Just flat.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in or enjoy doing?

Not really, no. I suppose... well, that's actually why my wife finally got me to agree to come in. I just don't care about the things that used to keep me balanced. Um... I used to do sailing races, and I had a Saturday shift at the historical society. I even liked tinkering in the woodshop. But now... it all just feels like chores. I just keep putting them off.
Have you been feeling anxious about anything lately?
Um... no. Not really. I mean, there's the usual stress from work, I guess, but... no. I wouldn't say I've been feeling anxious about anything.
Do you think the feeling of things being a chore is because you've lost interest in them or because you just don't feel good when you're doing them?

Um... I don't know if there's much of a difference, really. I just... I don't feel much of anything. Like... my wife and kids can be laughing at dinner, or I'll finish a difficult project milestone at work. And I know those things should feel good. But... they don't. I mostly just feel flat. Kind of... removed from it all, I guess.
Have you ever had a period of time where you felt really down or depressed for most of the day?
Um... no. Not really. I mean, I feel flat, like I said, but... I wouldn't say I feel down or depressed. Just... tired, maybe. But not depressed.
Are there any activities that you used to enjoy but now no longer find pleasure in?

Yeah... I suppose so. Honestly, that's kind of what finally made me agree to come in here. I just... I don't really care about the things that used to keep me balanced. 

Um... like the sailing races, or my Saturday shift at the historical society. Even just tinkering out in the woodshop. It all just... feels like a chore now. Just things I keep putting off.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight over the past year?
Um... no. Not really. My weight's been pretty steady.
Have you had periods of feeling depressed in the past that lasted for a couple of weeks or more?
No. I don't think so. I've never really been the depressed type... so, no.
Do you feel like you no longer enjoy things that you used to find pleasurable?
Um... yeah. I think we just talked about that. Like I said a minute ago... the sailing, the woodshop. I just don't really have the interest I used to. So... yes.
Have you ever had a period of feeling depressed that lasted for two weeks or more before the past year?
Um... no. Like I just said a minute ago, I've never really been depressed. Not before this past year, not ever, really. So... no.
Do you feel any physical pleasure or enjoyment when you are engaged in activities, even if you don't feel like doing them?

Um... not really. I mean... even if I'm doing something, it's just... I don't know. Like, my wife and kids can be laughing at dinner, or... or I'll finish a difficult milestone on a project at work. I know those things should feel good, but... mostly I just feel flat. Kind of... removed from it, I guess.
Do you feel any pleasure or enjoyment when you are engaged in social activities with your family?
I mean... I think I just answered that. Like I was just saying about sitting at dinner with my family... I just feel flat. So... no, not really.
Do you ever feel sad?
Not really. I mean... I wouldn't call it sad. Just... like I said, kind of flat. I don't really feel much of anything.
Have you experienced any feelings of worthlessness?
No... I wouldn't say that. I don't feel worthless. I just... go to work, do my job. I just don't feel much of anything.
Have you experienced any periods where your flat mood was worse than it is now?
Not really. It's... I don't know, it just stays about the same. Just always kind of like this.
How long have you been feeling this flat mood without any significant improvement?
A little over a year, I guess. Ever since... well, since the scaffold accident. Back during the business readjustment. It's just been like this since then.
Would you say that this flat mood of yours is mild, moderate, or severe?
I don't really know. I guess... maybe mild? I haven't really thought about how to rate it. It's just... there.
